issues.body: In _evaluate_main, an empty PR_NUMBER makes fetch_pr_draft None, and resolve_eval_tier(..., None) unconditionally returns full. The workflow deliberately permits PR_NUMBER to be empty by swallowing failure of the same-SHA PR lookup with `|| true`; its own comments also say fork workflow_run payloads lack the PR number. For a pull_request-triggered run, an API failure or unresolved association therefore publishes ci-gate (including on the requested seed path) without establishing that the PR is ready. A draft PR could consequently receive the eventual required context from its reduced matrix. The existing test_no_pr_is_full_tier covers merge_group only and misses this real wiring path.
issues.fix_hint: Preserve whether the triggering event is pull_request. If it is and no PR number can be resolved, return an unknown tier and publish nothing; only merge_group/non-PR events may infer full tier from the absence of a PR. Add an integration-level unit test driving the empty-PR_NUMBER pull_request path (or a refactored helper) and assert that neither requested nor completed evaluation publishes ci-gate. Consider making the resolver step fail explicitly or emit a resolved/unresolved signal instead of erasing lookup errors with `|| true`.
issues.title: Unresolved pull-request identity defaults to full tier

verdict.summary: The slotless evaluator has a fail-open draft-tier path. When a pull_request workflow_run payload does not provide a PR number and the fallback PR lookup fails or returns no result, the workflow passes an empty PR_NUMBER. The evaluator then treats the absence of a draft probe as full tier and may publish the required ci-gate context for a draft head. This contradicts the documented no-information/no-write invariant and is not covered by the added tier tests.
